messages:
IncidentBot: paging @Rohit Jain (on-call) — severity: P1. High error rate to inference endpoints in us-west-2b, elevated 502/504s, Route53 weighted routing flapping detected :rotating_light:
Rohit Jain: I'm on it. grabbing context and runbook. anyone seeing console alerts for ELB target health?
Maria Chen: getting the ELB health metrics now — target unhealthy counts spiked ~00:12 UTC, latency for volumes attached to hosts in us-west-2b also high.
Zara Patel: AWS health page shows an "EC2 networking disruption" for us-west-2b in the advisory feed. link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/ — looks regional and limited to one AZ.
Ajohnson: quick customer impact note: about 8% of production traffic is routed to us-west-2b; API 3xx/4xx counts mostly normal, but 502/504 on generation endpoints; embedding jobs retried and some timed out.
Rohit Jain: running targeted checks: 
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:xxxx:targetgroup/rl-infer-ecs-tg
```
Rohit Jain: TG shows ~30% unhealthy in us-west-2b, healthy in a/c. logs show socket timeout to local EC2 instances.
Infra Tilly: EBS latency alarms firing for a subset of instances in us-west-2b — I can push a temp autoscaling detach for affected instances.
Maria Chen: We should switch weighted Route53 routing to favor other AZs/regions while we mitigate. Suggest change: shift weight off us-west-2b -> us-west-2a/c (immediate) and enable cross-region failover to us-west-1 for critical routes.
Zara Patel: We have a weighted routing record for api.redwood-inference.com, TTL 60. Manual change should propagate quickly.
Ajohnson: I'll prepare the DNS change. posting the terraform one-liner I'm about to run:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2b","Weight":1,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.0.0.111"}]}}]}'
```
CustomerOps: tagging incident with customer-impact: partial for production clusters in us-west-2. sending proactive comms to customers on regen latency.
Rohit Jain: made the interim DNS update to reduce weight to us-west-2b to 5% and increased us-west-2a/c to 47/48. verifying metrics now.
IncidentBot: Route53 change propagated, change id C1234567890.
Maria Chen: after shift, observed 65% drop in 504s from external synthetic canaries. backend error rate still elevated for jobs pinned to us-west-2b.
Zara Patel: Can we enable ELB cross-zone load balancing and lower healthcheck threshold to reduce flapping?
Rohit Jain: enabling cross-zone LB now and increasing healthy threshold to 3 -> 2 to let healthy targets serve while we replace bad instances.
Ajohnson: also preparing an ASG replace-instances-by-launch template for nodes with EBS latency; will drain and replace instances reporting i/o stalls.
Infra Tilly: starting instance replacement in us-west-2b. command: 
```
aws autoscaling attach-instances --instance-ids i-0abc... --auto-scaling-group-name rl-infer-asg --no-should-exist
```
Rohit Jain: rolling replacements started, switching heavy inference traffic to reserve capacity in us-west-1 for the next 30 minutes via routing policy.
CustomerOps: sending customer update draft for approval: "We detected elevated request failures to a subset of nodes in us-west-2b. We shifted traffic and are replacing impacted hosts; mitigations in place and performance recovering." approve? :thumbsup: / :thumbsdown:
Maria Chen: :thumbsup: send it. include link to status page and ETA ~1h for full recovery.
Zara Patel: monitoring: 504s trending down, EBS latency alarms decreasing as replacement completes.
Rohit Jain: note for postmortem: need extra runbook step to pre-populate weighted DNS fallback for cross-region and possibly reduce DNS TTL on critical entries during high-change windows.
Ajohnson: capture the terraform change and route53 change id in the incident log.
IncidentBot: escalation: agent on-call for infra team: @Infra Tilly acknowledged.
Infra Tilly: replacement finished for 6 instances; they're reporting healthy, seeding KV caches back now.
Maria Chen: KV cache warmup causing a short burst of latency for some requests — fallback cache serving enabled.
Rohit Jain: handing off to day on-call: @Zara Patel will monitor and own mitigation progress for next 4 hours. summary: we shifted weights off us-west-2b, replaced bad instances, enabled cross-zone LB, and routed critical traffic to us-west-1 temporarily. customer impact: partial (8% of traffic) reduced to minimal. next steps: validate cold-cache behavior, follow up with AWS support for EBS incident correlation.
Zara Patel: acknowledged, will watch dashboards and update status page every 15m.
CustomerOps: posted customer note and opened support tickets for customers with high error spikes.
Rohit Jain: attaching quick runbook actions for handoff: 
- check Route53 weights and change status id C1234567890 
- confirm ELB target health in all AZs 
- confirm ASG replacement completed and EBS latencies back to baseline
- coordinate with AWS support case 987654321

Rohit Jain: thanks all. closing the active paging loop — leave open for monitoring. :white_check_mark:
